# Rollout Plan: Migrating 40,000 Users from Legacy Billing to New Billing System

## Overview

This plan migrates 40,000 existing users from the old billing system ("Legacy") to the new billing system ("Nova") in controlled phases. Both systems will run in parallel (dual-write / shadow mode where applicable) for the duration of the rollout, giving each phase a safe fallback path. The old system is **not** decommissioned as part of this plan — decommissioning is explicitly deferred to a separate post-migration phase, at least one full billing cycle after the final batch completes, so that any billing disputes, refunds, or invoice corrections still have a system of record to reconcile against.

---

## Phase 0: Pre-Migration Readiness (0% of users migrated)

**Purpose:** Validate infrastructure, tooling, and rollback mechanisms before any real user is touched.

- **% of users:** 0% (internal/synthetic test accounts only, plus up to 50 opted-in internal employee accounts)
- **Entry criterion:** New billing system (Nova) has passed a full parallel reconciliation test against Legacy using replayed production-shaped invoice data for 14 consecutive days with zero unexplained discrepancies; automated rollback tooling (reverting a migrated account back to Legacy as billing system of record) has been tested successfully on at least 20 synthetic accounts; on-call runbook and dashboards are published.

---

## Phase 1: Pilot Cohort ("Canary")

- **% of users:** 1% (~400 users), selected from low-risk segments: month-to-month plans, no active disputes, no enterprise/custom contracts, opted into beta communications.
- **Entry criterion:** Phase 0 exit criteria met and signed off by Billing Eng Lead and Finance; incident response rotation staffed for the duration of the pilot; customer support team briefed and provided with a migration-specific FAQ/playbook.
- **Duration:** Minimum 2 full billing cycles (to observe at least two invoice/renewal events per migrated user) before proceeding.

## Phase 2: Expanded Rollout ("Early Majority")

- **% of users:** 15% cumulative (~6,000 users), expanding to include mid-tier plans and a limited number of annual-plan users, still excluding enterprise/custom-contract accounts.
- **Entry criterion:** Phase 1 completed its full duration with zero Sev-1/Sev-2 billing incidents attributable to Nova; invoice-amount discrepancy rate stayed below the halt threshold (see Metrics below) throughout; support ticket volume related to billing did not increase more than 10% over Phase 1 baseline.

## Phase 3: General Availability Migration ("Majority Rollout")

- **% of users:** 60% cumulative (~24,000 users), opening migration to all remaining standard self-serve and mid-market accounts, still excluding highest-complexity enterprise contracts.
- **Entry criterion:** Phase 2 exit metrics green for 2 consecutive weeks; finance month-end close using Nova-sourced data for migrated cohort reconciled successfully against Legacy for at least one full close cycle; data retention/compliance sign-off obtained for expanded PII/payment data volume in Nova.

## Phase 4: Final Batch — Long Tail & Enterprise ("Completion")

- **% of users:** 100% cumulative (remaining ~16,000 users, including enterprise/custom-contract accounts, dunning/at-risk accounts, and any accounts held back due to edge-case billing logic).
- **Entry criterion:** Phase 3 exit metrics green for 2 consecutive weeks; each enterprise account has an individually reviewed migration runbook signed off by both Billing Eng and the named Customer Success/Account Manager; legal/contractual review confirms no custom contract terms are incompatible with Nova's billing logic.
- **Important constraint:** Legacy system remains fully operational, unmodified, and undeleted during this phase and for a defined post-migration soak period afterward (minimum 90 days / one full quarterly billing cycle) before any decommissioning activity is even planned. Decommissioning of Legacy is explicitly out of scope for this rollout plan and will be tracked as a separate initiative with its own approval gate.

---

## Halt / Rollback Metrics

The rollout is **automatically paused** (no further accounts migrated to the next phase or cohort) if any of the following occur, and requires Billing Eng Lead + Finance sign-off to resume:

- **Invoice discrepancy rate > 0.5%** of migrated accounts in any rolling 24-hour window (defined as invoiced amount on Nova differing from the Legacy-computed shadow invoice by more than $0.01 or 0.1%, whichever is greater).
- Payment failure rate for migrated cohort exceeds baseline (Legacy) payment failure rate by more than **2 percentage points** in any 7-day window.
- Billing-related support ticket volume for migrated users exceeds **3x** the pre-migration per-capita baseline in any 48-hour window.

---

## Risks

RISK: Duplicate or double billing occurs when both Legacy and Nova attempt to charge the same customer during dual-run | Implement a single source-of-truth flag per account gating which system is authorized to initiate charges, enforced via a shared idempotency/lock service checked by both systems before charge execution | Billing Platform Eng Lead
RISK: Proration and mid-cycle plan-change logic differs between Legacy and Nova, causing incorrect invoice amounts for migrated users | Run shadow-mode parallel invoice generation for every migrated account for at least one full cycle and automatically flag any diff above threshold for manual review before the invoice is sent | Billing Data/QA Lead
RISK: Enterprise customers with custom contract terms (custom pricing, negotiated discounts, non-standard billing cycles) are migrated before Nova fully supports their contract logic, causing revenue leakage or contract breach | Require explicit per-account migration checklist and sign-off from Customer Success/Account Management before any enterprise account leaves Phase 3, with enterprise accounts held in Legacy until verified | VP Customer Success / Enterprise Billing Owner
RISK: Rollback of a migrated account back to Legacy mid-cycle causes loss or duplication of billing history, confusing customers and finance reporting | Build and test a bidirectional sync/rollback tool in Phase 0 that preserves a full audit trail and reconciles partial-cycle charges before switching system of record back | Billing Platform Eng Lead
RISK: Customer support is unprepared for billing questions from users mid-migration, leading to poor customer experience and escalations | Provide support team with migration cohort visibility (which system each account is on), a dedicated FAQ/playbook, and a fast-track escalation path to the billing migration on-call engineer | Head of Customer Support

PHASES: 5
